title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The orders and indices in the diagram check out: GL_2(Z/4) has order 96, SL_2(Z/4) 48, the kernel of reduction 16, A_4 12, D_Q 8, and the abelianisation has order 4.

Slight notational ambiguity in the last displayed isomorphism. GL_2(Z/4) has centre of order 2, so it cannot be a direct product S_4 × F_2^2. The final '(Gl(M_0).M_0) • F_2^ω' must therefore be read as a semidirect product, consistent with the earlier '1/2 direct' remark, not as a direct product.
Gl_Λ(M)' cannot be the commutator subgroup, which has order 24. It must denote Gl/𝔷 = PGL_2(Z/4) or Ker(sg·det), both of order 48. The notation is unexplained on the page.
The label 𝔖_J^+ on the bracket near Sl/(M_0×𝔷) is loose. Sl_Λ(M)/(M_0×𝔷) has order 6 ≅ S_3 = 𝔖_J, whereas 𝔖_J^+ = A_3 has order 3. The bracket is probably meant for a different quotient.

ideas.what: Subgroup lattice of GL_2(Z/4) with indices, cartesian squares, and quotients identified with S_3, D_4, C_4
ideas.modern_name: structure of GL_2(Z/4Z) / level-4 congruence quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke; standard finite group theory)

ideas.what: Intrinsic labelling of the three index-2 characters (det, sg, sg·det) by canonical F_2-torsors μ = Or(M), ω, ω∧μ
ideas.modern_name: canonical (choice-free) description of the abelianisation of GL_2(Z/4); torsor bookkeeping

ideas.what: PGL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4 × Z/2 ≅ Aut(octahedron on P^1(Z/4))
ideas.modern_name: octahedral symmetry of X(4) / cusps of level 4
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (modular curve of level 4 and the octahedron)

ideas.what: Splittings of the extensions depend on a trivialisation of a torsor P_M ('half-splitting' of M)
ideas.modern_name: non-canonical splitting of the congruence extension 1→(1+2M_2)→GL_2(Z/4)→GL_2(F_2)→1

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, choice-free bookkeeping of the well-known group GL_2(Z/4) and its octahedral action, in Grothendieck's characteristic intrinsic style. It is correct and pleasant but mathematically classical; nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'μ ≃ (Λ^3 M)^*' should read '(Λ^2 M)^* = Or(M)'. M has rank 2, and the superscript is a 2.
The '{+C_Q+}' over ω is an annotation 'ω ≅ C_Q', not an insertion.
Read 'où Δ est l'octaèdre non orienté de sommets Δ = M^*/±1', not 'orienté [?] ; M de sommets Δ = M^+/±F_2'.
The left bracket labels are 𝔖_I (outer) and '𝔖_J ≃ Gl_{F_2}(M_0)' (inner).
NB sentence is likely: 'les cinq carrés qui y apparaissent (dont certains composés?) sont cartésiens. On a marqué sur chaque flèche l'indice dans l'inclusion des sous-groupes qu'elles représentent.'
'Ker(sg.det) ≃ 𝔖_I × F_2' — the F_2 has a subscript/decoration that is hard to read; likely 𝔷 or F_2.
